name: The Reading Room
verdict: The stone-and-log storeroom massing and mossy plinth are a good start, but the heavy flat deepslate cap, the busy front where you can't tell door, window and shutters apart, and the gate pieces floating off the corner keep it from reading as a lived-in reading room.

log.verdict: The materials work well together (log corners, stone brick, spruce infill, deepslate) and the barrel, lantern and bookshelf window read correctly, but the roof is a flat, heavy deepslate lid with no gable or overhang, the entrance is muddled by several door-like panels, and the garden gate shows up as loose trapdoors and fence bits floating by the plinth, so at a glance it reads as a squat box with clutter.

log.n: task 1: Make the garden gate read as a gate
task 2: Add a roof eave lip on the front and bac
task 3: Chimney on the west gable
task 4: Hang a second small sign by the barrel
task 5: Moss and cracks at the base
task 6: Window surrounds in deepslate on every s
task 7: Curtains on the side and back windows
task 8: Operator touch: clean quartz doorstep
task 9: Interior: floor rug and warm light
task 10: Fix walkability readout and door reveal
